summary: High tail latency and intermittent request timeouts from SDK clients caused by small connection pool + aggressive retry policy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports increased 5xx/timeouts and a long right-tail on inference latency starting 2026-02-19 morning. Impact: production traffic for several critical endpoints experienced user-facing slowdowns and occasional request failures leading to downstream transaction retries. Hypothesis early: client-side connection pooling and retry/backoff interaction causing serial queueing and replays that amplify perceived platform latency.
timeline: 2026-02-19 08:00 UTC - first signs of tail latency in customer's telemetry; 2026-02-19 09:15 UTC - customer opens support; 2026-02-20 10:30 UTC - support confirmed patterns consistent with connection pool saturation; 2026-02-22 14:00 UTC - reproduced in staging with default SDK config; 2026-02-24 11:00 UTC - mitigation applied and monitoring updated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy client using redwood-js-sdk v1.4.3 with default settings (connectionPool.max=2, keepAlive=false, retryCount=6)
2) Fire 200 concurrent short requests that produce small token outputs (avg 30 tokens) at ~100 rps
3) Observe request queueing at the client layer and multiple repeated attempts for single user requests
4) Inspect client connection metrics: long wait_for_connection times and frequent TCP teardown/recreate
5) Compare to same test with connectionPool.max=16 and keepAlive=true to note reduced perceived latency and fewer retries
logs: [sdk] 2026-02-19T08:05:12Z DEBUG retrying request attempt=3 backoff_ms=1200 trace_id=abc123
investigation_notes: Reproduced the client's symptom in our staging environment by using the same SDK version and default config. Observed client-side serialized requests: connectionPool.max=2 caused N concurrent app threads to wait for connections leading to long client wait times and retries.

SDK v1.4.3 default changed in PR #987: increased retryCount and aggressive exponential backoff jitter introduced more replay attempts when connections were slow to obtain. This amplifies client queueing under short-request, high-concurrency workloads.

HTTP/2 multiplexer misconfiguration not primary; most reproductions used HTTP/1.1 and showed clear per-host connection limits causing serial queuing. When keepAlive=true and pool max increased, tail latency dropped by ~70%.

No server-side capacity shortage observed: serving runtime metrics show steady CPU/GPU utilization and low token-level processing time. Error budget correlated with request timeouts initiated by the client, not 5xx from backend.

Customer's dedicated setup used an internal LB that terminated keepalives aggressively (idle timeout 20s) which increased socket churn and made connectionPool ineffective unless enabled with keepAlive.
impact: Customer-facing slowdowns for Inkling Financial morning batch windows, intermittent user transaction failures. Perceived platform reliability hit; customer escalated to platform SLA team.
comments: Customer (Samir Rao): 'We started seeing a flurry of timeouts and then a steady stream of retries. Our UX shows spinning indicators for minutes.'
Support (Aisha Patel): 'Requesting SDK config and connection metrics. Can you confirm SDK version and whether keepalive is enabled on your LB?'
Customer (Samir Rao): 'Using redwood-js-sdk v1.4.3 via our node microservice. LB timeout is 20s, default SDK settings otherwise.'
SRE (Nina Torres): 'Observed client_wait_ms spikes in API ingress logs matching customer request windows. No backend saturation.'
SDK Eng (Marco Nguyen): 'We have a patch to change defaults and expose pool sizing guidance in README. Preparing patch PR 1012.'
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied 2026-02-24: advised customer to upgrade to redwood-js-sdk v1.4.4 (hotfix) that enables keepAlive by default and reduces retryCount to 3. Customer applied change and reported reduced tail latency within 30 minutes.

Recommended configuration for high-concurrency, short-response workloads: connectionPool.max >= concurrency / 8 (empirical), keepAlive=true, retryCount <= 3, baseBackoff<=200ms. Example: connectionPool.max=16, keepAlive=true, retryCount=2 for 200 client threads.
Longer-term fixes: SDK default change merged (PR 1012) to sensible defaults for production workloads and expanded SDK docs with a 'connection pool sizing' section and runbook linked in Confluence.
Added an alert to platform ingress: client_wait_ms P95 > 500ms -> create ticket and surface client-side queueing to support during triage.
Follow-up: schedule a proactive run with top dedicated customers to review SDK settings and LB keepalive timeouts.
Follow-up internal task created: INT-4218 to add end-to-end tests for connection churn and retry amplification scenarios.
final_status: Mitigated - customer applied SDK hotfix and config guidance; monitoring in place. Follow-up tasks assigned.
